Modified read with SLOOS and Beige Book insights:
- Policy stance: A hawkish pause. The FOMC held the funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and continued balance-sheet runoff, emphasizing cumulative tightening, policy lags, and vigilance on inflation risks. Inflation is easing but still elevated; job gains have moderated; tighter financial and credit conditions are expected to weigh on activity.

- SLOOS lens: Banks reported further tightening and weaker demand across key credit channels (C&I, CRE, consumer, and residential mortgages), citing higher funding costs, deposit competition, liquidity concerns, and collateral/value issues. This reinforces that bank credit will be a drag on growth beyond the baseline statement.

- Beige Book cross-check (New York District): Reports point to easing employment demand and softer labor market conditions, mixed-to-weaker consumer spending, moderating inflationary pressures, soft housing markets, and inventory adjustments. These observations corroborate slowing activity and easing price pressures noted by the FOMC, while reinforcing a cooler demand backdrop.

Implications: Combined SLOOS and Beige Book signals tilt the balance of risks further toward slower growth and softer hiring, even as inflation continues to ease. While the banking system remains resilient and inflation progress supports eventual policy normalization, the near-term growth impulse looks weaker than a statement-only read.

Net tone: modestly more negative than before due to concurrent credit tightening and Beige Book-confirmed softening in demand and housing.
